key_insight: Microstructure-dependent recurrent neural operators can approximate homogenized Kelvin–Voigt viscoelastic laws in 2D and 3D, with a sufficient internal-variable dimension growing logarithmically in inverse relative stress error and material contrast.
engineering_relevance: These surrogates aim to replace costly concurrent unit-cell simulations while generalizing across loading histories and microstructures.
method: Use internal variables to approximate loading-history dependence through a Markovian state.
Represent microstructure-dependent constitutive responses with neural operators.
Use the homogenized memory kernel’s spectral representation to establish uniform approximation guarantees and dimension bounds.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments on viscoelasticity and crystal plasticity examine internal-variable dimension and sample complexity; the theoretical results are formally verified in Lean 4.
watch_item: The approximation guarantees apply to periodic Kelvin–Voigt viscoelasticity; crystal plasticity is explored numerically rather than covered by the stated theory.
paper_title: Operator Learning of Microstructure-Dependent Internal-Variable Models for Inelastic Homogenization: Approximation and Complexity
